description: Hygienic Macro System (M15) — compile-time defmacro with syntax objects, quasiquoting, scope-mark hygiene, and introspection/construction APIs

userStories.title: Add JACL_TAG_SYNTAX value tag and OBJ_SYNTAX GC object
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need a value type to represent AST nodes as manipulable values during macro expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: Add JACL_TAG_SYNTAX to the tag enum in value.c (use next available 5-bit tag slot)
Add OBJ_SYNTAX to the GC object kind enum in gc.c

JaclSyntax struct in jacl.h: uint8_t kind (enum mapping to AST node types), SourcePos pos, uint32_t scope_mark, plus a union for per-kind data: command (head JaclVal + args JaclVal vec), lit_int (int32_t), lit_float (float), lit_string (JaclVal string), var_ref (JaclVal name string), block (JaclVal vec of syntax commands), spread (JaclVal child syntax), interp_string (JaclVal vec of segments)
GC tracing in gc_collect.c traces all JaclVal fields inside JaclSyntax (head, args vec, name, commands vec, child, segments vec)
GC sweep handles OBJ_SYNTAX
Helper macros: jacl_is_syntax(val), jacl_as_syntax(val)
Allocation: gc_alloc_syntax(heap) returns a new JaclSyntax*
Syntax objects print readably via value printing: <syntax:command [...]>, <syntax:lit-int 42>, etc.
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Kind enum values: SYNTAX_COMMAND, SYNTAX_LIT_INT, SYNTAX_LIT_FLOAT, SYNTAX_LIT_STRING, SYNTAX_VAR_REF, SYNTAX_BLOCK, SYNTAX_INTERP_STRING, SYNTAX_SPREAD, SYNTAX_USE, SYNTAX_DEFSTRUCT, SYNTAX_BREAK, SYNTAX_CONTINUE, SYNTAX_RETURN, SYNTAX_DESTRUCTURE_VEC, SYNTAX_DESTRUCTURE_NAMED

userStories.title: AstNode to syntax object conversion
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to convert parsed AstNode trees into syntax object values for macro bodies to manipulate.
acceptanceCriteria: New function JaclVal syntax_from_ast(AstNode* node, GCHeap* heap) in a new file src/syntax.c
Recursively converts all AstNode types to corresponding syntax objects
AST_COMMAND: head converted, each arg converted, stored in a vector
AST_LIT_INT, AST_LIT_FLOAT, AST_LIT_STRING: datum stored directly
AST_VAR_REF: name stored as JaclVal string
AST_BLOCK: each command converted, stored in a vector
AST_INTERP_STRING: each segment converted, stored in a vector
AST_SPREAD: child converted
AST_BREAK, AST_CONTINUE, AST_RETURN: value (if any) converted
AST_ERROR nodes cause a compile error (not convertible)
Source positions (line, col) copied from AstNode to syntax object
All scope marks initialized to 0 (no macro context)
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: AST_USE and AST_DEFSTRUCT conversion can use a simplified representation (store field names/types as vecs of strings). AST_DESTRUCTURE_VEC and AST_DESTRUCTURE_NAMED similarly store names/types as vecs.

userStories.title: Syntax object to AstNode conversion
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to convert syntax objects back into AstNode trees for bytecode compilation after macro expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: New function AstNode* syntax_to_ast(JaclVal syntax, arena_t* arena) in src/syntax.c
Recursively converts all syntax object kinds back to AstNode types
SYNTAX_COMMAND: allocates AST_COMMAND with converted head and args
SYNTAX_LIT_INT, SYNTAX_LIT_FLOAT, SYNTAX_LIT_STRING: allocates corresponding AST_LIT_* nodes
SYNTAX_VAR_REF: allocates AST_VAR_REF with name from syntax datum
SYNTAX_BLOCK: allocates AST_BLOCK with converted commands
Source positions round-trip: AstNode -> syntax -> AstNode preserves line/col
Test: parse a program, convert to syntax, convert back to AST, pretty-print both — output matches
Test: round-trip with nested commands [if [> $x 3] { print $x }]
Test: round-trip with block containing multiple commands
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Scope marks on syntax objects are not preserved in AstNode — they are used during expansion for hygiene, then discarded. The compiler's name resolution uses scope marks from the syntax objects during expansion, before converting back.

userStories.title: Lexer and parser support for defmacro
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to parse defmacro declarations into AST nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: TOKEN_DEFMACRO added to lexer keyword table in lexer.c
AST_DEFMACRO added to AstNodeType enum in ast.c
AST_DEFMACRO data: name (string), param_names (array of strings), param_count (uint32_t), body (AstNode* block)
Parser handles: defmacro name {param1, param2} { body }
Parser error if defmacro appears inside a block (not at top level)
Parser error if defmacro has no name, no param block, or no body block
Pretty-printer handles AST_DEFMACRO
Test: parse defmacro unless {cond, body} { syntax-quote [if [not ~cond] ~body] } produces correct AST
Test: defmacro inside a proc body produces parse error
Test: defmacro with zero params: defmacro now {} { ... }
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: At parse time, the body is parsed as a normal block — quote, syntax-quote, ~, ~@ are handled later by the compiler. The parser just needs to recognize defmacro as a top-level form.

userStories.title: Lexer and parser support for quote
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to parse quote expressions into AST nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: TOKEN_QUOTE added to lexer keyword table in lexer.c
AST_QUOTE added to AstNodeType enum in ast.c
AST_QUOTE data: child (AstNode* — the quoted expression)
Parser handles: quote <expr> where expr is any single expression (command, literal, var-ref, block)
quote does not recurse into its argument — the child is stored as-is
Pretty-printer handles AST_QUOTE: prints as quote <child>
Test: parse quote [+ 1 2] produces AST_QUOTE wrapping AST_COMMAND
Test: parse quote $x produces AST_QUOTE wrapping AST_VAR_REF
Test: parse quote { print 1; print 2 } produces AST_QUOTE wrapping AST_BLOCK
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: Lexer and parser support for syntax-quote, ~, and ~@
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to parse syntax-quote templates with unquote holes into AST nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: TOKEN_SYNTAX_QUOTE added to lexer keyword table
TOKEN_TILDE (~) and TOKEN_TILDE_AT (~@) added to lexer as punctuation tokens
AST_SYNTAX_QUOTE added to AstNodeType enum — data: child (AstNode*)
AST_UNQUOTE added to AstNodeType enum — data: child (AstNode* — the expression to evaluate)
AST_UNQUOTE_SPLICING added to AstNodeType enum — data: child (AstNode*)
Inside a syntax-quote context, parser recognizes ~ prefix on expressions as AST_UNQUOTE
Inside a syntax-quote context, parser recognizes ~@ prefix on expressions as AST_UNQUOTE_SPLICING
Nested syntax-quote: inner syntax-quote increments depth, ~ only unquotes at depth 0
Parser error if ~ or ~@ appears outside syntax-quote
Pretty-printer handles all three new node types
Test: parse syntax-quote [if [not ~cond] ~body] — AST_SYNTAX_QUOTE with AST_UNQUOTE children
Test: parse syntax-quote [foo ~@args] — AST_UNQUOTE_SPLICING for args
Test: ~ outside syntax-quote produces error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: ~ only works in structural positions (command args, block commands), NOT inside strings. ~@ only valid in command arg lists or block command lists.

userStories.title: Compile-time macro table and defmacro registration
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to register macro definitions in a compile-time table so the expansion pass can look them up.
acceptanceCriteria: New MacroTable struct in compiler.c: maps macro name (string) to a compiled macro entry
MacroEntry struct: name, param_count, param_names, compiled body (JaclClosure*)
When compiler encounters AST_DEFMACRO: compile the body block to bytecode as a closure, register in macro table
The macro body closure receives syntax object parameters and returns a syntax object
Error if macro name shadows a special form (if, proc, def, mut, set, while, for, match, etc.)
Error if macro name is already registered (duplicate defmacro)
Macro table is consulted during expansion pass to check if a command head is a macro call
Test: defmacro registers in table, lookup by name succeeds
Test: defmacro shadowing 'if' produces compile error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: The macro body is compiled eagerly when defmacro is encountered (top-to-bottom order). This means it can only reference macros/procs defined above it.

userStories.title: Macro expansion pass — basic expansion
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need a pass that walks the AST, identifies macro calls, and replaces them with expanded syntax.
acceptanceCriteria: New function ast_expand_macros(AstNode** program, uint32_t count, MacroTable* macros, GCHeap* heap, arena_t* arena) in src/syntax.c
Walks AST top-to-bottom; for each AST_COMMAND, checks if head is a bare word matching a macro name
When a macro call is found: convert each argument to a syntax object, call the macro closure with those syntax objects, convert the returned syntax object back to AstNode, replace the call node
Non-macro commands pass through unchanged
Blocks: recurse into each command in the block
Expansion is iterative — after replacing a node, re-walk the result for further macro calls
Depth counter incremented per expansion, error at 256 with message: 'macro expansion depth limit exceeded in expansion of <name>'
Expansion pass runs after parsing, before the existing compilation pass
Test: defmacro unless {cond, body} { syntax-quote [if [not ~cond] ~body] } then unless [eq 1 2] { print ok } expands to [if [not [eq 1 2]] { print ok }]
Test: depth limit hit by self-referencing macro produces clear error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: The expansion pass needs a VM instance to execute macro bodies. Reuse the compiler's embed VM or create a dedicated expansion VM.

userStories.title: Compiler handling of quote — emit syntax object literal
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to compile quote expressions into bytecode that produces syntax object values.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler handles AST_QUOTE: converts the child AstNode to a syntax object at compile time, emits it as a constant
The syntax object is added to the bytecode chunk's constant pool
At runtime (during macro body execution), the quote expression pushes the syntax object onto the stack
Nested quotes: quote [foo quote [bar]] produces a syntax object containing a syntax object for the inner quote
Test: inside a macro body, quote [+ 1 2] produces a syntax object with kind command, head +, args [1, 2]
Test: quote $x produces a syntax object with kind var-ref, name x (not a variable lookup)
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: quote is only meaningful inside macro bodies (compile-time code). Outside macros it could be allowed as a general-purpose form, but for now it only needs to work during expansion.

userStories.title: Compiler handling of syntax-quote — template expansion
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to compile syntax-quote templates into bytecode that builds syntax objects with unquoted holes filled in.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler handles AST_SYNTAX_QUOTE: generates bytecode that constructs a syntax object tree at runtime (during macro body execution)
Literal parts of the template become syntax object constants (like quote)
AST_UNQUOTE (~) children: compile the inner expression normally, result must be a syntax object, splice it into the template position
AST_UNQUOTE_SPLICING (~@) children: compile the inner expression, result must be a vec of syntax objects, flatten into the surrounding command args or block commands
Runtime error if ~ result is not a syntax object
Runtime error if ~@ result is not a vec of syntax objects
Nested syntax-quote depth tracking: inner syntax-quote treated as literal (not expanded)
Test: syntax-quote [if [not ~cond] ~body] with cond and body bound to syntax objects produces correct compound syntax
Test: syntax-quote [foo ~@args] with args = vec of 2 syntax objects produces 3-arg command
Test: ~@ in block position: syntax-quote { ~@stmts } flattens vec of syntax into block
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: syntax-quote compiles to a sequence of bytecode instructions that allocate and assemble syntax objects. This is more complex than quote — it's a mix of constants and evaluated expressions.

userStories.title: End-to-end basic macro test
userStories.description: As a Jacl programmer, I want to define and use a simple macro that works end-to-end from source to execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: defmacro unless {cond, body} { syntax-quote [if [not ~cond] ~body] } followed by unless [eq 1 2] { print ok } prints ok
Test: defmacro double {x} { syntax-quote [+ ~x ~x] } followed by double 21 returns 42
Test: macro that expands to another macro call works (two-level expansion)
Test: macro used before its defmacro produces compile error with clear message
Test: macro with wrong argument count produces compile error
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: This is the integration test story that validates US-001 through US-010 working together. If earlier stories were tested in isolation, this validates the full pipeline.

userStories.title: Scope marks on syntax objects for hygiene
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need scope marks on syntax objects so that macro-introduced identifiers don't collide with caller identifiers.
acceptanceCriteria: Global scope mark counter (uint32_t, starts at 1) incremented each time a macro expansion begins
When syntax-quote builds a syntax object, all var-ref and def/mut/set target identifiers get the current macro's scope mark
When ~ splices a syntax object, it retains its existing scope marks (the caller's)
syntax_to_ast preserves scope marks as metadata on AstNode (add uint32_t scope_mark field to AstNode struct)
Compiler name resolution: two identifiers match only if same name AND same scope mark (0 matches 0 for non-macro code)
Test: defmacro m {x} { syntax-quote { tmp = 1; [+ ~x $tmp] } } then tmp = 99; m $tmp returns 100
Test: two nested macro expansions each introducing tmp don't collide
Test: non-macro code (scope mark 0) works exactly as before
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Scope mark 0 means 'no macro context' — all existing non-macro code has scope mark 0, so existing name resolution is unchanged. The scope mark field on AstNode is only populated for macro-expanded code.

userStories.title: ^ prefix for intentional binding introduction
userStories.description: As a macro author, I want ^name in syntax-quote to introduce a name in the caller's scope for anaphoric macros.
acceptanceCriteria: Inside syntax-quote, ^identifier parsed as a special unquote variant that creates an identifier with scope mark 0 (caller's scope) instead of the macro's scope mark
Parser recognizes ^ prefix on bare identifiers inside syntax-quote context
The resulting var-ref syntax object has scope mark 0 regardless of the current expansion's scope mark
^ only valid inside syntax-quote — compile error elsewhere
Test: defmacro aif {cond, body} { syntax-quote { ^it = ~cond; if $^it ~body } } then aif 42 { print $it } prints 42
Test: ^ used outside syntax-quote produces compile error
Test: ^name doesn't collide with a macro-internal name of the same string
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: Scope mark 0 means caller's scope. This works because the caller's code has scope mark 0 (or whatever the enclosing context's mark is). For nested macros, ^ should use the immediate caller's scope mark, not necessarily 0 — this may need refinement.

userStories.title: gensym builtin
userStories.description: As a macro author, I want gensym to generate unique symbol names for temporaries.
acceptanceCriteria: gensym registered as a native builtin available during macro expansion
gensym takes one optional string argument (prefix), default prefix is 'g'
Returns a syntax object (var-ref kind) with a name like prefix__gN where N is a global counter
Generated names contain characters that are not valid in user-written identifiers (the __ separator ensures no collision with user names)
Each call increments the counter — names are globally unique across all macro expansions
Test: [gensym tmp] called twice produces two distinct syntax objects
Test: macro using gensym for a temporary doesn't collide with caller's variable of the same prefix
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra
userStories.notes: gensym is simpler than scope marks for the common case of macro-internal temporaries. Both mechanisms coexist — scope marks handle hygiene automatically, gensym is explicit.

userStories.title: Introspection builtins
userStories.description: As an advanced macro author, I want to inspect syntax object structure.
acceptanceCriteria: syntax-kind: takes a syntax object, returns the kind string (command, var-ref, lit-int, lit-float, lit-string, block, interp-string, spread, use, defstruct, break, continue, return, destructure-vec, destructure-named). Error if arg is not a syntax object.
syntax-datum: returns raw value for literals (i32 for lit-int, f32 for lit-float, string for lit-string), name string for var-ref. Error for other kinds.
syntax-head: returns head syntax object for commands. Error for non-commands.
syntax-args: returns vec of arg syntax objects for commands. Error for non-commands.
syntax-commands: returns vec of command syntax objects for blocks. Error for non-blocks.
syntax-pos: returns a map with line and col keys (i32 values).
syntax->string: returns pretty-printed string representation of the syntax tree.
All 7 builtins registered as native functions available during macro expansion.
Test: syntax-kind on quote [+ 1 2] returns command
Test: syntax-head on quote [+ 1 2] returns syntax object for +, syntax-datum on that returns +
Test: syntax-args on quote [+ 1 2] returns vec of 2 syntax objects
Test: syntax-pos returns correct line/col
Test: each builtin errors clearly on wrong type
All existing tests pass
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra

userStories.title: make-syntax construction builtin

Test: macro using make-syntax to conditionally build different AST
